title: Specified cone arrows and common-stage Verdier structure for the older presentation
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and any scheme $Y$; no structure map from $Y$ to $k$ is assumed. Let $I$ be the finite coefficient subfields of $\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. For $E\in I$, fix the small model $\widetilde E=\mathrm{Shrink}(E)$ and its algebra equivalence $s_E:\widetilde E\cong E$, and put $i_{EL}=s_L^{-1}\circ(E\hookrightarrow L)\circ s_E$. Let $\mathcal A_E^{\mathrm{old}}$ be the full subcategory of the completed integral derived category whose objects are derived complete and whose reductions modulo every positive uniformizer power are finite-torsion constructible in a single finite cohomological interval independent of the power [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Here the specified presentation is exactly $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegralCategory}(D,\ell,\ell\ne p,\widetilde E,Y)$, with its functors $\mathrm{integralDerivedReduction}$. Set $C_E^{\mathrm{old}}=\mathcal A_E^{\mathrm{old}}[1/\varpi_E]$, the raw Hom scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], namely $\mathrm{rationalConstructibleCategory}(D,\ell,\ell\ne p,\widetilde E,Y)$. Its scalar transition $T^{\mathrm{old}}_{EL}$ is $\mathrm{rationalScalarExtension}$ along $i_{EL}$. These named presentations specify the categories and maps in the assertions below; no identification with a different presentation of the integral predicate is asserted.

Equip $P^{\mathrm{old}}$ with the system, Hom groups and shifts of [lem-pur-general-legacy-stage-coherence, lem-pur-general-legacy-hom-coordinates, lem-pur-general-legacy-pair-shifts]. The given scalar transitions are exact [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated]. There is a unique pretriangulation on these fixed data in which the distinguished triangles are precisely the triangles isomorphic to distinguished finite-stage images; it is triangulated and the inclusions $j_L$ are exact [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data, def-weil-triangulated-category]. More precisely, let $A=(E,K)$, $B=(F,H)$, $L\ge E,F$, and let
$$U=(T^{\mathrm{old}}_{EL}K\xrightarrow{u}T^{\mathrm{old}}_{FL}H\xrightarrow{g}C\xrightarrow{h}(T^{\mathrm{old}}_{EL}K)[1])$$
be distinguished in $C_L^{\mathrm{old}}$. Write $\delta_A:A\cong j_LT^{\mathrm{old}}_{EL}K$ and $\delta_B:B\cong j_LT^{\mathrm{old}}_{FL}H$ for the specified stage identifications. There is a distinguished triangle with literal objects $A,B,(L,C)$ and arrows
$$[L,u],\quad j_L(g)\circ\delta_B,\quad \delta_A^{-1}[1]\circ\beta_{L,1,T^{\mathrm{old}}_{EL}K}\circ j_L(h).$$
Its isomorphism to $j_L^\triangle U$ has components $\delta_A,\delta_B,1_{(L,C)}$.

source.note: Construction material from old argument 8 (retained verbatim): For the retained finite-field legacy realization: Apply the existing common-stage Verdier theorem to obtain the pretriangulation, exact inclusions and distinguished criterion. For a given finite-stage cone, form its image triangle and conjugate its first two objects by isoToStage. The representative identity gives its prescribed first arrow; Triangle.isoMk proves it distinguished with the literal third pair unchanged. Exactness, the Hom node and the shift node supply every hypothesis of lem-route-common-stage-verdier-exists-unique, with the general directed-stage data, not the geometrically restricted PBC definition. For the displayed cone apply j_L to U. Set the second arrow to delta_B followed by j_L(g), and the connecting arrow to the stage image connecting arrow followed by the shift of delta_A inverse. The first triangle-isomorphism square is mkHom_eq_isoToStage; the second is the identity-unit equation; the third cancels the shifted inverse of delta_A. Triangle.isoMk supplies the isomorphism with identity on the third object. The common-stage distinguished criterion gives the result. The same literal cone argument is also the retained old argument 4: A commonStageCone is isomorphic to the image of its supplied distinguished finite-stage triangle. Its three isomorphism components are isoToStage for the first two objects and the identity for the third. The first arrow equation is mkHom_eq_isoToStage, the second is a unit equation, and the connecting arrow equation cancels the shifted inverse identification. Apply distinguished_iff.

proof.text: For every $E$, apply [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] to the specified derived-complete, uniformly bounded-reduction subcategory $\mathcal A_E^{\mathrm{old}}$. By [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear] it is $\mathcal O_E$-linear with linear shift. Apply [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] with $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi=\varpi_E$. It gives a triangulated structure, including TR4, on the raw localization $C_E^{\mathrm{old}}$, with precisely the stage shift and stage distinguished triangles used here. All three cited statements allow any scheme $Y$.

proof.text: The coefficient index is nonempty and directed by [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. The specified tensor system is supplied by [lem-pur-general-legacy-stage-coherence]. Its fixed Hom-group laws and additive inclusions are supplied by [lem-pur-general-legacy-hom-coordinates]. The zero object, additive integer shifts, coherent inclusion comparisons and shift-compatible $\theta$ are supplied by [lem-pur-general-legacy-pair-shifts]. Exactness of the specified transitions is [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated]. These are exactly the hypotheses of the exact-stage pair datum [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]; no unitor $T_{EE}=1$ is required. Together with step 1, they meet every hypothesis of [lem-route-common-stage-verdier-exists-unique]. Apply it on these fixed data. This gives the unique pretriangulation, the common-stage distinguished criterion, TR4 and exactness of every $j_L$, with the already prescribed comparisons.

proof.text: We compute the first arrow from the quotient formulas of [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Put $X=T_{EL}K$, $Z=T_{FL}H$, $a_A=\alpha_{ELL,K}$ and $a_B=\alpha_{FLL,H}$. The representatives of $\delta_A$, $j_L(u)$ and $\delta_B^{-1}$ at $L$ are respectively $a_A^{-1}$, $T_{LL}(u)$ and $a_B$. Their composite therefore has class $[L,a_B T_{LL}(u)a_A^{-1}]=[L,t(u)]$, where $t$ is reflexive transport on this Hom set. This equals $[L,u]$: the cocycle with indices $(E,L,L,L)$ gives $T_{LL}(a_A)=\alpha_{LLL,X}$ after cancellation of $a_A$, and similarly for $a_B$. Naturality of $\alpha_{LLL}$ then gives $t(t(u))=a_B\alpha_{LLL,Z}T_{LL}^2(u)\alpha_{LLL,X}^{-1}a_A^{-1}=t(u)$. Thus the two representatives $t(u)$ and $u$ have equal transports at $L$ and define the same quotient class. In particular $j_L(u)\circ\delta_A=\delta_B\circ[L,u]$. This calculation uses no faithfulness and no identity-transition assumption.

source.place: Retained old arguments 4 and 8: mkHom_eq_isoToStage, with reflexive-stage transport made explicit.

proof.text: Let $V=j_L^\triangle U$. By [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data], its connecting arrow is $w=\beta_{L,1,X}\circ j_L(h)$. Define a triangle $W$ with literal objects $A,B,(L,C)$ and arrows $f=[L,u]$, $g_W=j_L(g)\circ\delta_B$, $h_W=\delta_A^{-1}[1]\circ w$. The types are $A\to B$, $B\to(L,C)$ and $(L,C)\to A[1]$. The triple $(\delta_A,\delta_B,1)$ is a triangle morphism $W\to V$: its first square is step 3, its second is $1\circ g_W=j_L(g)\circ\delta_B$, and its third is $\delta_A[1]\circ h_W=w\circ1$ by functoriality of $[1]$ and $\delta_A\delta_A^{-1}=1$. By [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift] this componentwise invertible triangle morphism is an isomorphism. Its inverse has components $(\delta_A^{-1},\delta_B^{-1},1)$, so the third object and third isomorphism component are literally as asserted.

proof.text: The distinguished $U$ and the isomorphism $W\cong j_L^\triangle U$ of step 4 witness $D_{S^{\mathrm{old}}}(W)$ in [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. The criterion obtained in step 2 therefore makes $W$ distinguished. Its three arrows are the displayed formulas by construction, and its isomorphism to the stage image has components $\delta_A,\delta_B,1_{(L,C)}$.
